questions.question: Ajmer Sharif is the shrine of which of the following Sufi saints?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti** is the Sufi saint associated with the shrine at Ajmer Sharif.
 
• Ajmer Sharif, located in Ajmer, Rajasthan, is one of the most prominent and revered Sufi shrines in India.
 
• Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti, also known as Gharib Nawaz, was a 13th-century Sufi saint and philosopher who founded the Chishti Order in India.
 
• The shrine attracts millions of pilgrims from different faiths, who come to seek the saint's blessings.
 
• Annual Urs festival commemorates the death anniversary of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti and is a major event at Ajmer Sharif.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti** was born in 1141 CE in Sistan (modern-day Iran) and moved to India in the early 13th century.
 
• He is known for his teachings of love, compassion, and service to humanity, which form the core principles of the Chishti Order.
 
• The shrine includes the saint's tomb, a mosque, and several other structures built by various rulers over centuries.
 
• Ajmer Sharif Dargah is also a symbol of communal harmony, where people from all religions and walks of life come together in reverence.
 
• The site is managed by the Dargah Committee, under the Dargah Khwaja Saheb Act of 1955.

questions.question: Chanakya was Prime Minister under the reign of ______ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandragupta Maurya.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chanakya**, often referred to as **Kautilya and Vishnugupta,** served as **prime minister during Chandragupta Maurya's rule, **the founder of the **Mauryan Empire.**
 
• His most famous work, the **political treatise Arthashastra, **was written as a guide for the youthful **Chandragupta** on how to rule successfully.
 
• He was** raised in Taxila **and was born into a **Brahman household.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Harshavardhana:**

 
 
• **From 606 until 647 CE, northern India** was ruled by the Indian ruler Harshavardhana.
 
• He belonged to the **Vardhana dynasty **and was** Prabhakaravardhana's son.**
 
 
 
• **Bindusara:**
 
 
• The **second Mauryan emperor of India** was Bindusara.
 
• He was the **father of Ashoka,** the dynasty's most well-known ruler, and the son of **Chandragupta, the dynasty's founder.**
 
 
 
• **Ashoka:**
 
 
• From roughly **268 to 232 BCE,** Ashoka, an Indian ruler of the** Maurya Empire **and the son of Bindusara, governed nearly the **entire Indian subcontinent.**

questions.question: Which Emperor adopted the Zabat System of measurement of land?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Sher Shah**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• Sher Shah started the** land measurement system** in India.
 
• Sher shah adopted the system of measurement of land known as zabt. This system

 continued till the time of 1579 that is in the twenty fourth year of Akbar’s rule.
 
• For land revenue** improvement, he determined the share in production based on the variety of land and crops.**
 
• Sher Shah started the application of **'Zarib' for land measurement.**
 
• Sher Shah fixed the area of a bigha** 360 square yards.**
 
• **On the basis of yield and category, the land was divided into three parts good, middling, and low.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Sher Shah Suri was the founder of the Suri Empire in India.**
 
• After taking control of the** Mughal Empire in 1540, **he set up a new civic and military **administration and implemented several reforms in the financial and postal** sectors. 
 
• The** famous Battle of Chausa was fought between him and the second Mughal Empire Humayun in the year 1539.**

questions.question: Which of the following books is related to "Principles of Buddha" ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Abhidhamma Pitta**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Abhidhamma Pitta** is one of the three main categories of texts in the Pali Canon of Theravada Buddhism.
 
• The Pali Canon is the standard collection of scriptures in the Theravada Buddhist tradition, preserved in the Pali language.
 
• It includes teachings attributed to the Buddha and his close disciples.
 
• The other two main categories of the Pali Canon are the **Vinaya Pitaka** and the **Sutta Pitaka**.
 
• The **Abhidhamma Pitaka** provides a detailed scholastic analysis and summary of the teachings found in the Sutta Pitaka.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Vinaya Pitaka** deals with the rules and regulations for the monastic community, including the disciplinary code for monks and nuns.
 
• The **Sutta Pitaka** consists of discourses attributed to the Buddha and some of his closest disciples.
 
• The Pali Canon is also known as the **Tipitaka**, which means "Three Baskets," referring to its three main divisions.
 
• Theravada Buddhism is one of the oldest forms of Buddhism and is practiced primarily in Sri Lanka, Thailand, Myanmar, Laos, and Cambodia.

questions.question: The Vijayanagar kingdom was established by _________ in 1336.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harihara and Bukka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Vijayanagar kingdom** was established by **Harihara and Bukka** in** 1336**.
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire, established in 1336, flourished in the **Deccan region of peninsular and southern India**.
 
• Founded by Harihara, also known as Hakka, and his brother Bukka Raya, the empire derived its name from its capital city, Vijayanagara, located in present-day Karnataka.
 
• **Vijayanagara district, **situated in the Indian state of Karnataka, lies within the Kalyana Karnataka region.
 
• It was established in 2020, emerging as the 31st district of the state after being carved out of Bellary district. The district's administrative center is Hosapete.
 
• Vijayanagara district encompasses the former capital of the illustrious Vijayanagara Empire, Hampi, which has been designated as a *UNESCO World Heritage Site*.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Venkatapati Raya,** from the Aravidu Dynasty, served as the third Emperor of the Vijayanagara Empire. He ascended to the throne following his older brother, Emperor Sriranga Deva Raya.
 
• **Deva Raya II **was a distinguished emperor of the Vijayanagara Empire, hailed as one of the most remarkable rulers of the Sangama dynasty. Known for his prowess in administration, warfare, and scholarship, he left a lasting legacy.
 
• **Krishnadevaraya, **a monarch of the Vijayanagara Empire from 1509 to 1529, was a prominent figure in Indian history. Belonging to the Tuluva dynasty, he is revered as one of the most illustrious rulers of India, renowned for his remarkable achievements during his reign.

questions.question: The Rig Veda consists of _____ hymns.
questions.solution:
**The Rig Veda consist of __1028__ hymns.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• There are **four vedas - **** the Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda and Atharvaveda.**
 
• The **oldest Veda is the Rigveda**, composed about 3500 years ago.
 
• The **Rigveda consists of 1028 hymns or suktas**.
 
• These hymns are in praise of various gods and goddesses.
 
• These hymns were **composed by sages** (rishis).
 
• Most of the hymns were composed, taught and learnt by men.
 
• A few were composed by women.
 
• The Rigveda hymns are **composed in old or Vedic Sanskrit**.
 
• 
 
The Rigveda is **divided into ten books **which are known as **Mandalas**.

 

Hence, the correct answer is - **1028.**__
